title: Pretomanid
dek: The Pa in BPaLM/BPaL: 200 mg daily, Ddn-activated nitroimidazole, not licensed as a solo DS drug, not for pregnancy. ZeNix/PRACTECAL made it a 6-month letter.
story: Pretomanid is a nitroimidazooxazine developed for TB, given 200 mg once daily in BPaLM/BPaL. Like delamanid, it needs Ddn and F420. Unlike DLM, it is the WHO-preferred 6-month nitroimidazole when the person is eligible — and unlike DLM, WHO explicitly does not apply the BPaLM recommendation to pregnant or breastfeeding people.
It is not a first-line DS-TB drug. It is not HPMZ’s P (that P is rifapentine). Letter collision has already harmed charting; write “pretomanid” on the medication list.

Hepatotoxicity, lactic acidosis (rare), and animal testicular toxicity drive some of the caution. Resistance network: ddn, fbiA–D, fgd1. Catalogue still thinner than for RIF. Prior nitroimidazole exposure is a reason to sequence the network before counting Pa.
deep: Nix-TB used LZD 1200 mg; ZeNix and PRACTECAL informed 600 mg LZD + Pa ± MXF. Operational BPaLM follows the later dose.
Pa is not approved as monotherapy; never “just add Pa” to HRZE.
If Pa is unavailable, that is an indication for BDLLfxC, not for skipping a nitroimidazole and hoping BDQ+LZD+MXF is the same trial.

visual.caption: Pretomanid’s allowed neighbourhood is small on purpose. Outside it, use DLM-based 6-month or other constructs — do not stretch Pa into pregnancy or DS-TB.

example.title: HPMZ labelled “Pa” in the EHR
example.setup: DS-TB on HPMZ. Medication list says pretomanid 1200 mg because someone mapped P → Pa.

steps.title: This is rifapentine 1200 mg
steps.body: HPMZ’s P is RPT. Pretomanid 1200 mg would be a toxicology event and the wrong disease class.

steps.title: Fix the name in the record
steps.body: Write rifapentine. Ban lone “P” in mixed DS/DR wards.

steps.title: Confirm the actual tablets
steps.body: Pharmacy, not the alias table, is the ground truth.

example.takeaway: Pretomanid is BPaLM’s Pa, 200 mg, gated — never HPMZ’s P.

choices: BPaLM/BPaL for eligible RR/MDR (and pre-XDR as BPaL)
